{{Quote|You don't last as a bounty hunter by judging your clients. I stick by that. Mostly.|The Hunter|<ref name="TOR:TOLB">{{TORcite|exp=shadow|type=class|Bounty Hunter|The Ones Left Behind|Rishi}}</ref>}}
The '''Hunter''', also known by the callsign '''Scree''', was the nickname of a famous [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] and [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]] that rose to prominence during the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]], winning the [[Great Hunt (competition)|Great Hunt]] [[Bounty/Legends|bounty]] hunting competition and earning the title of '''Grand Champion of the Great Hunt'''. Inducted into the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorians]] by [[Mandalore the Vindicated]] himself, the Hunter pursued dangerous bounties on the legendary [[Blacklist]], but became one of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy's]] most wanted after the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] issued warrants for the bounty hunter's arrest based on trumped-up charges. In the service of the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Tormen]], the Hunter lured out and eliminated the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Jun Seros (Jedi)|Jun Seros]], who was responsible for the charges, and also [[Assassin/Legends|assassinated]] [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Dorian Janarus]] themselves. With the charges cleared, the Hunter continued to serve the Sith Empire as one of its premier mercenaries during the [[Galactic War]].

==Biography==
===Early years===
{{Quote|Best shot I've ever seen and nerves of steel. He's Great Hunt material, all right.|[[Braden]]|<ref name="Gauntlet">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|Gauntlet|Hutta}}</ref>}}
The Hunter rose to prominence in a time of great [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] upheaval. The [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]] brought about resumed hostilities between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|resurgent Sith Empire]] following the breaking of the [[Treaty of Coruscant]], which had ended the [[Great Galactic War]] some eleven [[Standard year/Legends|years]] earlier. Due to the diplomatic nature of fighting an undeclared war, the Empire utilized hired [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenaries]] and bounty hunters without hesitation to accomplish much of its goals. This practice carried over into the [[Galactic War]].<ref name="HoloNetBH">{{Holonet|classes|bounty-hunter|Bounty Hunter}}</ref>

Three [[Great Hunt (competition)|Great Hunts]] were held during this eleven-year period. The Hunter participated in [[Great Hunt (c. 3643 BBY)|the last]] of these. Their main rival would become [[Tarro Blood]], who participated in a [[Great Hunt (c. 3653 BBY)|hunt]] ten years earlier, and was badly beaten by his fellow competitors after they united against him. The previous hunt was won by [[Jewl'a Nightbringer]].

===Entering the Hunt===
====Braden's protégé====
{{Quote|Every bounty hunter who's won a Great Hunt went on to massive glory and riches--which is why we're here.|Braden|<ref name="Gauntlet" />}}
[[File:Braden.png|thumb|left|150px|Braden discovered the Hunter and became the protégé's mentor.]]

{{GameDSmechanics|Star Wars: The Old Republic}}
During the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]], the Hunter was scouted by a veteran bounty hunter named [[Braden]] who decided to take the talented young mercenary in as his protégé. Arriving on [[Nal Hutta/Legends|Nal Hutta]], the Hunter was introduced to the other members of Braden's team: [[Mako (slicer)|Mako]], a talented slicer, and [[Jory]], a strong [[Nikto/Legends|Nikto]] who was responsible for security. Braden planned on getting his protégé into the [[Great Hunt (competition)|Great Hunt]], a competition held for bounty hunters across the galaxy. There were two ways to gain sponsorship: One either had to become a [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]], a process that would take too long considering the competition was nearly beginning, or gain the favor of a powerful [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]]. As it so happened, [[Suudaa Nem'ro]] was one who had not yet sponsored a hunter. Running their base of operations out of the [[Poison Pit]] [[Cantina/Legends|cantina]] in the [[City/Legends|town]] of [[Jiguuna]], which was embroiled in a war between [[Nem'ro's gang|Nem'ro's forces]] and [[Fa'athra clan|those]] of [[Voontara Fa'athra]], the team began to search for ways to get the Hunter noticed by the powerful [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]].<ref name="Gauntlet" />

Since Braden had dealings with Nem'ro in the past, he was able to secure an introduction for the Hunter, but first Mako would need to forge rumors of the Hunter's exploits across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. In addition, the Hunter would need to take down a difficult target to prove his worth. Mako found that a disreputable [[Corellian/Legends|Corellian]] fugitive named [[Vexx]] was in town. The Hunter raided Vexx's safe house, finding nothing but his henchmen and a [[Datapad/Legends|datapad]], which Mako was able to slice, cracking the encryption to reveal that Vexx planned to take a shuttle off-planet.<ref name="Gauntlet" /> Arriving at Jiguuna's spaceport just before Vexx escaped, the Hunter engaged him in combat and won, [[Death/Legends|killing]] him. Upon returning to the Poison Pit, the Hunter discovered the bodies of Braden and Jory in their room at the cantina. Examining the room's [[Holorecorder/Legends|holorecording]], the Hunter and Mako learned that the two were killed by [[Sedyn Kyne]] on the orders of [[Tarro Blood]], depriving the Hunter of the support needed to enter the Great Hunt. While the Hunter went to speak with Nem'ro about securing his sponsorship, Mako gave Jory and Braden a proper burial in the planet's swamps.<ref name="LastFlight">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|The Last Flight|Hutta}}</ref>

====Earning sponsorship====
[[File:SuudaaNemro-SWTOR.png|thumb|right|190px|Nem'ro the Hutt became the Hunter's sponsor.]]
{{Quote|You want sponsorship in the Great Hunt. I can provide that. But why should I? Mako says you are a famous bounty hunter--that hardened men run and hide just hearing your name. But Mako says many things. You want to prove that you are this fearsome manhunter? I will give you that chance.|Nem'ro, upon meeting the Hunter.|<ref name="BigChief">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|Big Chief|Hutta}}</ref>}}
Before arriving at [[Nem'ro's Palace]], the Hunter eliminated two prominent leaders of Fa'athra's forces that were holed up in Jiguuna, threatening the security of Nem'ro's rule. Upon meeting the Hunter, Nem'ro praised them for their assistance against Fa'athra, but voiced skepticism about the Hunter's true abilities. To sell their reputation, the Hunter would need to bring Nem'ro the head of an [[Evocii]] known as [[Huttsbane]], the leader of a violent uprising against the Hutts on the planet. The Hunter complied with the order, killing the Evocii and his clan. Mako reported to the Hunter via [[Holocomm/Legends|holocomm]] that she had confirmed the identity of Braden's killer as Tarro Blood, and that she had been followed by a suspicious [[Kaleesh/Legends|man in a bone mask]]. She also discovered that Blood was paying off other [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorians]] so they wouldn't gang up on him like they did in the previous Great Hunt.<ref name="BigChief" />

The Hunter returned to Nem'ro's Palace with Huttsbane's head, delivering it before the Hutt to the sound of his approval.<ref name="BigChief" /> Before acquiring payment from a [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] named [[Juda]], the Hunter was briefed by Nem'ro on the next bounty for a man named [[Yalt]], one of Nem'ro's former [[Accountant/Legends|accountants]] who had betrayed him for Fa'athra at [[Yalt (female)|his wife's]] suggestion. The Hunter tracked Yalt to one of Fa'athra's factories in the [[Rust Yards]] of Nal Hutta and, after heavy fighting through Fa'athra's forces, cornered him. Though Yalt begged for mercy, even offering a bribe, the Hunter declined, killing Yalt and taking the man's head to his wife.<ref name="SettlingAccounts">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|Settling Accounts|Hutta}}</ref>

Upon returning to Nem'ro's throne room, the Hunter was approached by a [[Rodian/Legends|Rodian]] bounty hunter named [[Nails]], who had been hired by Tarro Blood. The Hunter threatened Nails, but she declined the chance to leave, and was killed by the Hunter.<ref name="SettlingAccounts" /> The Hunter then confirmed their kill with Nem'ro, who asked him to go kill his beast keeper, claiming he was a traitor and was plotting against the Hutt. This turned out to be a trick&mdash;the keeper released a series of beasts upon the Hunter, who slayed them all. The keeper then attacked the Hunter, and was killed.<ref name="HouseCleaning">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|House Cleaning|Hutta}}</ref>

[[File:Mako1.png|thumb|left|150px|Mako accompanied the Hunter, driven by her desire to avenge Braden's death.]]

After the Hunter returned to Nem'ro and told him of the beast keeper's death, the Hutt informed them then that he had already sponsored someone for the Great Hunt. Nem'ro told the Hunter if they wanted the [[sponsorship token]], they should find the bounty hunter and take it from him, which angered the Hunter. Mako approached the Hunter after their meeting with Nem'ro, and asked to accompany them on the Great Hunt in exchange for the name and location of the bounty hunter. The Hunter agreed, and Mako revealed the identity of the bounty hunter–a fierce and deadly [[Trandoshan/Legends|Trandoshan]] named [[Rarsk]]. Mako had intercepted a transmission between Rarsk and the bone-masked man, and found out that Rarsk was on his way to [[Fa'athra's Palace]] to claim a bounty the Hutt had been holding for him, a Republic scientist named [[Albea]]. The two set out for Fa'athra's palace, determined to find Rarsk's bounty before him and set a trap for the rival hunter. They arrived at the palace, located Albea, and waited for Rarsk to arrive. When Rarsk entered the palace, he confronted the Hunter and Mako and demanded they hand over the scientist. The Hunter did not comply and killed the Trandoshan, claiming his sponsorship token. The Hunter then took in Albea for the bounty, which Mako argued against.<ref name="MySponsorship">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|My Sponsorship|Hutta}}</ref>

Returning to Nem'ro, they found the bone-masked man that had been following Mako, and learned that he was actually a Great Hunt representative named [[Grataa]]. He accepted the Hunter into the Great Hunt, and Mako and the Hunter were allowed to travel to Dromund Kaas and join the melee that would decide who entered the Great Hunt.<ref name="MySponsorship" />

====First bounty====
{{Quote|Today, we have too many hunters. All must compete. Only one joins the Great Hunt!|The Huntmaster addressing the sponsored bounty hunters.|<ref name="TheHuntmaster">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|The Huntmaster|Dromund Kaas}}</ref>}}
Arriving on the Imperial Fleet,<ref name="EscapingHutta">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|Escaping Hutta|Hutta}}</ref> the Hunter and Mako took a [[Shuttle/Legends|shuttle]] to [[Dromund Kaas/Legends|Dromund Kaas]], the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] capital of the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]].<ref name="TheHuntonDromundKaas">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|The Hunt on Dromund Kaas|Hutta}}</ref> There, the two met up with their handler at the [[Mandalorian enclave]], [[Crysta Markon]]. Markon told them there was only one spot remaining in the Great Hunt and over three dozen sponsored hunters left. The [[Huntmaster (Wookiee)|Huntmaster]] then gathered the hunters into the main room and informed them they would be competing for a spot in the final melee, requiring them to turn in three bounties or be disqualified. The winner of the final melee would go on to be entered into the Great Hunt.<ref name="TheHuntmaster" /> The Hunter returned to Markon to receive their first bounty, a Republic [[Noble/Legends|noble]] named [[Altaca]] who was captured during an Imperial raid and accidentally sold into slavery. His slave group was building a [[Unfinished colossus|statue]] of [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Vowrawn]] when they [[Dromund Kaas rebellion|rebelled]] and took over the site. Altaca's [[Altaca family|family]] had posted the bounty with the hope of recovering him alive.<ref name="MustyTrail">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|A Musty Trail|Dromund Kaas}}</ref>

Searching for clues at the slave camp near the site, Mako and the Hunter found a datapad belonging to Altaca that contained a holocomm from Imperial noble [[Lady/Legends|Lady]] [[Dak-Ah]]. In it, she described a plan to use the slave uprising as a distraction to rescue Altaca, and afterwards he would pose as her missing brother. Mako traced the communication back to the [[Nexus Room]] cantina, where the two were confronted by [[Sergeant/Legends|Sergeant]] [[Wallax]]. He demanded that the Hunter and Mako surrender their weapons and gear before being interrupted by a holocomm from Tarro Blood. Blood asked the Sergeant if he had disposed of the Hunter yet and, after seeing they were still alive, scolded Wallax. After Wallax closed the communication, the Hunter gunned him down along with his freelance troopers. The Hunter then confronted Altaca and Lady Dak-Ah and called the pair on their bluff. Lady Dak-Ah attempted to strike a new deal with the Hunter, but they refused and killed her before capturing Altaca with the [[S86k full-gauge carbonite armor upgrade|S86k]]. The Hunter and Mako then returned to the Mandalorian enclave and turned in their first bounty to Markon.<ref name="MustyTrail" />

====Second bounty====
{{Quote|Your second bounty's a bit of a mystery. Apparently whoever's stacking the deck against you gonna keep right on stacking.|Crysta Markon to the Hunter|<ref name="MustyTrail" />}}
The second bounty assigned to the Hunter was a classified request from [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Fraabaal]] of the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]]. The Hunter and Mako went to Fraabaal's office and, after being initially accosted by [[Lieutenant/Legends|Lieutenant]] [[Petrak]], were granted an audience with the Admiral. Fraabaal revealed to them that his daughter, [[Vereta Fraabaal]], was the apprentice of [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] [[Grathan]], a [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] that had disgraced the [[Dark Council]]. The Dark Council was planning a raid against Lord Grathan, and if Fraabaal's daughter was either captured or killed by them, everyone in her family would suffer. Therefore, the Admiral considered her a liability, and requested the Hunter infiltrate Grathan's compound and kill his daughter.<ref name="FamilyCleansing">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|Family Cleansing|Dromund Kaas}}</ref>

The Hunter and Mako traveled to [[Lord Grathan's estate]] and located Vereta, who had been expecting them. Vereta told the Hunter that Grathan's spies had found out about the bounty her father placed on her head and began boasting about her abilities. She then expressed disappointment that a real Mandalorian hadn't been sent to kill her, and afterwards they engaged in combat. The Hunter prevailed over the [[Sith apprentice/Legends|Sith apprentice]], who was in disbelief over her defeat. Vereta claimed she was Sith and couldn't fall to a common bounty hunter before being executed by the Hunter. Mako and the Hunter returned to Admiral Fraabaal and collected payment for the bounty before receiving their next assignment from the Mandalorian enclave.<ref name="FamilyCleansing" />

====Third bounty====
{{Quote|Here we go. Bounty three. I call it: Someone's got a serious hate for my hunter.|Crysta Markon, while assigning the Hunter's final bounty.|<ref name="FamilyCleansing" />}}
The final bounty Markon had for the Hunter was from [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Medle]] of [[Imperial Intelligence/Legends|Imperial Intelligence]]. The Hunter and Mako went to the [[Ministry of Intelligence (Sith Empire)|Ministry of Intelligence]] and spoke to the Captain, who told them of a dormant [[Dark Temple|ancient Sith Temple]] that had recently started exhibiting signs of Sith sorcery. As a result, entrance to the Temple was restricted, but [[Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[Gargun]] had secretly led a team into the Temple to investigate. Nobody returned, and Medle wasn't able to report the missing soldiers without revealing the mission. Medle wanted the Hunter to go to the Temple and retrieve the ID tags from Gargun and his missing team so he could create more "acceptable" deaths for them and be promoted to Commander. The Hunter accepted and they made their way to the Dark Temple.<ref name="SpyGame">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|The Spy Game|Dromund Kaas}}</ref>

The Hunter and Mako found the missing soldiers inside the Temple, but the soldiers were possessed by the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark-side]] energy permeating the Temple. The duo killed the possessed soldiers and took their ID tags before encountering Commander Gargun, who had been possessed by the [[Force ghost/Legends|spirit]] of Sith Lord [[Barel-Slathborn]]. The spirit inquired as to who stood before him, but the Hunter simply pulled their blaster and attacked the possessed Commander. After a short skirmish, the Commander was dead and the Hunter took his ID tag before reporting back to the Ministry of Intelligence. Medle praised their performance, but told the Hunter he couldn't risk the Sith finding out they went into the Temple, and were now a liability. Captain Medle called his guards to his side, but the Hunter and Mako dispatched them with ease. Injured and defeated, Medle told them he wouldn't beg and handed over payment for the bounty, saying the rest was up to them. The Hunter told the Captain he had made a big mistake and killed him before returning to the Mandalorian enclave and turning in the last bounty.<ref name="SpyGame" />

====Final melee====
{{Quote|Enough! You hunters are the best that the galaxy's goons and thug lords could send us. Now show us which one of you will join the Great Hunt. Fight!|Assistant Huntmaster Lek to the remaining bounty hunters, just before the Final melee|<ref name="TheMelee">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|The Melee|Dromund Kaas}}</ref>}}
The Hunter and Mako returned to Markon, much to the handler's surprise. Tarro Blood had tried to sabotage the Hunter and told the Huntmaster that they had perished inside the Dark Temple. Markon said the final melee was about to begin and told the Hunter to hurry to the battle room. The Hunter arrived and joined the surviving bounty hunters just before the final melee started. Of the five bounty hunters that were left, none were a match for the Hunter, who emerged victorious from the final melee. Afterwards, as the Huntmaster was accepting the Hunter into the Great Hunt, Blood interrupted the proceedings and demanded that the Hunter not be allowed into the competition, claiming their credentials had been fabricated by Mako. [[Lek]], the Huntmaster's assistant, refused Blood's request, who then threatened to report the information to the Mandalore. Blood then threatened the Hunter directly before he left, proclaiming their skull would be in his hands before the Great Hunt was finished. The Huntmaster finished inducting the Hunter, and afterwards the Hunter and Mako reported to Markon to receive their first target of the Great Hunt.<ref name="TheMelee" />

===The Great Hunt===
Crysta then instructed the Hunter to steal a [[D5-Mantis Patrol Craft]] from the spaceport, but Blood had alerted the port authorities to the upcoming theft. But not even that could stop the Hunter, who killed the Imperials and the ship's [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidian]] [[Unidentified smuggler (Dromund Kaas)|owner]].<ref name="TOR:JR">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|Joy Ride|Dromund Kaas}}</ref>

====Balmorra====
{{Quote|Welcome to Balmorra, hunter. Your target is the right impressive Admiral Ivernus, they call him "Admiral Untouchable." Spends all his time on a fancy flagship surrounded by armed soldiers. Can't kill what you can't touch, hunter. You gotta lure Admiral Ivernus off his flyin' fortress and down to Balmorra.|[[Crysta Markon]]|<ref name="TOR:TBT">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|The Balmorran Target|the D5-Mantis}}</ref>}}
[[File:Pirrell.png|thumb|right|180px|Lieutenant Major Pirrell]]
The target for the Great Hunt on [[Balmorra/Legends|Balmorra]] was [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Ivernus]], an important Imperial officer casually known as "Admiral Untouchable," the reason being that he always oversees the conflict on the planet from his own starship. For that reason, the Bounty Hunter had to lure him down to Balmorra if they had any chance of eliminating him. Crysta was unable to provide the Bounty Hunter with a friendly contact on Balmorra, though Mako managed to find out that [[Lieutenant Major]] [[Pirrell]], one of Ivernus' subordinates, was in need for a bounty hunter.<ref name="TOR:TBT" />

Down on Balmorra in the Imperial-controlled city of [[Sobrik]], the Hunter was accosted by the siblings of the Corellian criminal Vexx, the Hunter's first target on Nal Hutta. [[Vorr (Corellian)|Vorr]] and [[Vye]] were told by Tarro Blood that the Hunter shot Vexx in the back and killed Braden when he discovered the Hunter's "crime". After dealing with them, the Bounty Hunter finally arrived at Lieutenant Major Pirrell's office.<ref name="TOR:PA">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|Pirrell's Ambitions|Balmorra}}</ref>

[[File:Ivernus.png|thumb|left|180px|Admiral Ivernus]]
The Hunter met with Pirrell and Murghir, a slavish [[Cathar/Legends|Cathar]] entertainment gift from one of Pirrell's friends on Dromund Kaas. Pirrell revealed the reason why he posted the request for a bounty hunter. He wanted his superior [[Colonel/Legends|Colonel]] [[Sartius]], whom he believed to be incompetent, discredited in the eyes of Admiral Ivernus and ousted from his position, to be taken be Pirrell himself. He planned to do this by humiliating Sartius by having the Bounty Hunter create problems that Sartius could not solve solve.<ref name="TOR:PA" /> He had the Hunter run jobs across Balmorra to that effort, dealing with battle droids in the [[Okara Droid Factory]],<ref name="TOR:CatDF">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|Chaos at the Droid Factory|Balmorra}}</ref> with [[Colicoid/Legends|colicoids]] in the [[Gorinth Canyon]],<ref name="TOR:DwtQ">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|Down with the Queen|Balmorra}}</ref> and with [[Balmorran resistance|Balmorran resistance fighters]] in the [[Balmorran Arms Factory]].<ref name="TOR:BaS">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|Bait and Switch|Balmorra}}</ref>

Once all three tasks were taken care of, Pirrell triumphantly reported that Sartius was placed under arrest and Ivernus was finally coming down to Balmorra. The Bounty Hunter seized this opportunity to get within blaster range of the admiral. The Bounty Hunter, Pirrell, and Murghir met up with Admiral Ivernus at the [[Sobrik Spaceport]]. However, much to Pirrell's surprise, instead of giving Pirrell a promotion, Ivernus came down to Balmorra to execute him in person for. Pirrell being in charge of intelligence, the admiral saw him as a worthless incompetent and ultimately considered Colonel Sartius's failures as Pirrell's own failures. However, as tension escalated, Murghir revealed her true face. She was a bounty hunter in the Great Hunt tracking the admiral as well, her dim-witted nature being all a ruse. A three-way battle soon erupted between the Hunter, Murghir, and Imperial forces. The Hunter was able to kill the admiral, his guards, and the rival bounty hunter, while the coward Pirrell was taking cover. After dealing with the terrified Lieutenant Major who begged for his life, the Bounty Hunter eventually departed Balmorra and set off for their next target.<ref name="TOR:MtA">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|Meeting the Admiral|Balmorra}}</ref>

====Nar Shaddaa====
{{Quote|It was a pleasure to meet you. Opponents like you are very rare--and precious.|[[Eidolon (assassin)|The Eidolon]], to the Hunter|<ref name="TOR:PC">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|Professional Courtesy|Nar Shaddaa}}</ref>}}
The Bounty Hunter's target on [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]] was called the [[Eidolon (assassin)|Eidolon]], a professional [[Assassin/Legends|assassin]] with the reputation for being able to kill anybody for the right price. His primary employer was the [[Hutt Cartel/Legends|Hutt Cartel]] until he retired and founded a successful security company: [[Eidolon Security]]. Many companies wanted to buy from Eidolon Security, costing the Hutt Cartel valuable customers. [[Gele'ren]], a lieutenant of the Hutt Cartel decided to wipe out Eidolon Security became the Bounty Hunter's contact on Nar Shaddaa. Down on the planet, the Hunter and Mako met Gele'ren in his office in the [[Slippery Slopes Cantina]], on the [[Promenade]]. Mako also reunited with [[Anuli]], an old friend who now worked for Gele'ren as a [[Slicer/Legends|slicer]]. Gele'ren revealed that Eidolon Security's primary client was the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], supplying the Republic military with billions of credits' worth of munitions every year.<ref name="TOR:TEoME">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|The Enemy of My Enemy|Nar Shaddaa}}</ref>

Gele'ren suggested the Bounty Hunter to anger the Eidolon into going after the Hunter, which is exactly what the latter wanted. The first step was to assault the Eidolon's [[Eidolon Armaments|weapon manufacturing facility]] in the [[Corellian Sector (Nar Shaddaa)/Legends|Corellian Sector]]. The Hunter destroyed crates of munitions, costing Eidolon Security billions of credits.<ref name="TOR:EB">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|Economic Boom|Nar Shaddaa}}</ref>

Gele'ren and the Bounty Hunter were discussing their next step in their plan when Mako localized the rival bounty hunters in the Great Hunt, the [[Zargnor Clan]], a trio of [[Ugnaught/Legends|Ugnaught]] named [[Gornik]], [[Slatblath]], and [[Ugmir]]. The Ugnaughts were building a new [[Battle droid/Legends|war droid]] in a [[Ugnaught Clan Warehouse|warehouse]] in the [[Duros Sector]]. The Bounty Hunter found the Ugnaughts in the empty building, still finishing their new war droid, fought them and eliminated them from the Great Hunt.<ref name="TOR:TU">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|The Underdogs|Nar Shaddaa}}</ref>

[[File:Eidolon2.png|thumb|right|200px|The Eidolon]]
After dealing with the Zargnor Clan, the next step in provoking the Eidolon was to get every confidential records of his customers into the public [[HoloNet/Legends|HoloNet]], where anyone can access. Anuli reported that the Eidolon's HoloNet transceivers were in the [[Network Access]] sector, heavily guarded and encrypted. The Bounty Hunter tracked down [[Zee K'lin]], a [[Bith/Legends|Bith]] engineer who has the access codes to the Eidolon's network. After striking the [[Nebula Communications security offices]], the Hunter found Zee at the [[Mezenti Spaceport]], preparing for departure, and acquired the Eidolon Security codes from him.<ref name="TOR:CZ">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|Catching Zees|Nar Shaddaa}}</ref> The Bounty Hunter then broke into the [[Eidolon Security datacenter]], and [[Mako (slicer)|Mako]] sliced into the company's secure database, transmitting its records to Anuli, who uploaded them onto the HoloNet.<ref name="TOR:IE">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|Industrial Espionage|Nar Shaddaa}}</ref>

When the Hunter and Mako returned to Gele'ren for updates, they discovered that Gele'ren and Anuli had been killed by [[Assassin droid/Legends|assassin droids]] sent by the Eidolon. The former assassin soon contacted the Hunter on the [[Holocomm/Legends|holocomm]] and revealed that he was responsible for the death of their partners. The Eidolon grew a strong respect for the Bounty Hunter and invited the Hunter to meet him face to face. The Hunter accepted the challenge and headed to the [[Eidolon's safe house]]. The Bounty Hunter faced the Eidolon to a duel, eventually becoming the victor. After the battle, Mako received a transmission that the Hutts would pay more for the Eidolon being captured alive, and the Bounty Hunter chose the target's fate, completing the bounty.<ref name="TOR:PC" />

====The auction====
{{Quote|The sanctity of the Great Hunt has been compromised. Seems a slicer got ahold of the Great Hunt's target list and intends to auction those names to the highest bidders. Exposure like that would destroy the Great Hunt. I need this dealt with quickly and discretely.|Huntsmaster Assistant [[Lek]]|<ref name="TOR:ADA">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|A Dangerous Auction|Hutta}}</ref>}}
After catching their first two marks, the Bounty Hunter was summoned to Dromund Kaas by Huntsmaster Assistant [[Lek]], who informed them that the list of Great Hunt targets had been stolen. The Bounty Hunter promptly departed to Nal Hutta where the list would be auctioned. The Hunter managed to interrupt the auction and killed the buyers, including [[Razak]] of the [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]]. The Hunter interrogated the seller, the slicer [[Bilikin Drell]], who revealed that the list was stolen by a Mandalorian. As the thief requested that Taro Blood's hits should be left confidential, the Hunter figured out that Blood had leaked the list to disadvantage his rivals. After retrieving the list and killing Drell, the Hunter returned to Dromund Kaas and received their next two targets, on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] and [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]].<ref name="TOR:ADA" />

====Sands of Tatooine====
[[File:Tyresius_Lokai.png|thumb|right|150px|Tyresius Lokai]]
{{Quote|I'm tired of running. My fortune's gone, but I'm still hunted. I want Tyresius Lokai dead as much as anyone. What if I told you there's a duplicate of yours truly? A replica identical in all respects? Even a bioscan couldn't tell the difference.|[[Gault Rennow|Tyresius Lokai]], to the Hunter|<ref name="TOR:CASE">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|Catching A Slippery Eel|Tatooine}}</ref>}}
The next target was a famous [[Devaronian/Legends|Devaronian]] fugitive named [[Gault Rennow|Tyresius Lokai]], who ran afoul of many criminal cartels. Tyresius was tipped off by Blood and attempted to escape [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] when its [[Tyresius Lokai's starship|starship]] was shot down over the desert<ref name="TOR:TTT">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|The Tatooine Target|D5-Mantis}}</ref> by the [[Rodian/Legends|Rodian]] bounty hunter [[Veeboo Lunx]]. However, the sly criminal paid off Lunx, who was eventually killed by the Hunter.<ref name="TOR:CV">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|Confronting Veeboo|Tatooine}}</ref> The Bounty Hunter then chased Tyresius around Tatooine,<ref name="TOR:ABwtLoP">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|A Barter with the Lady of Pain|Tatooine}}</ref> and eventually cornered the Devaronian at his ship. Lokai pleaded for his life and offered a compromise: the Hunter could shoot a double as proof that the Bounty Hunter got their mark and Tyresius could work for the Hunter. The fugitive promised to use all his resources in helping the Hunter who accepted the proposal. Under a new pseudonym, Gault Rennow, the Devaronian joined the crew of the Hunter.<ref name="TOR:CASE" />

====The Durasteel Duke====
The fourth target was Duke [[Corwin]], a.k.a. the Durasteel Duke. The Hunter sought out the assistance of the [[House Girard]] in tracking down Corwin. On the search, the Hunter broke into the Alde Royal Museum after acquiring the information that the Duke was communicating with [[House of Organa/Legends|House Organa]] via messages hidden there. Upon returning to [[Baron/Legends|Baron]] [[Zacar Girard]] it was discovered that Corwin was forming an alliance of multiple houses, consisting of some vassals of the [[House of Thul]] and [[House Ulgo]] and House Organa itself, against House Thul. They also found out, that the "Durasteel Duke" was under protection of [[House Rist]]. The Hunter then decided to break into the [[House Rist (estate)|Rist estate]].<ref>{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|Like a Rancor in a Pottery Shop|Alderaan}}</ref>

The Duke, however, left the estate only moments before the Hunter was able to infiltrate it and fled to [[Castle Organa]]. [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] [[Maddor Rist]] then contacted the Hunter via [[Hologram/Legends|hologram]] and presented him a job offer to kill all of House Girard. The Hunter accepted.<ref>{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|Silver Tongues|Alderaan}}</ref>

The Hunter ultimately cornered the Duke at an Organa estate. But much to the Hunter's surprise, Corwin was discovered to be dead and his sister [[Muriel Corwin]] was posing as him. The Organas then handed over Corwin's body.<ref>{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|Kingmaker for a Day|Alderaan}}</ref>

====Return to Nar Shaddaa====
{{Quote|Go to Nar Shaddaa. Confront those who have dishonored you and my people. Show them what it means to be a true warrior.|[[Hedarr Soongh]], to the unter|<ref name="TOR:HR">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|Honor Regained|Nar Shaddaa}}</ref>}}
[[File:Hedarr_Soongh_and_Sedyn_Kyne.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Hedarr Soongh confronts Sedyn Kyne.]]
The Hunter was soon contacted by [[Hedarr Soongh]], a previous Champion of the Great Hunt, who informed the Hunter that Blood's allies are gathering on Nar Shaddaa to discuss how to deal with the Hunter. The Hunter and Mako came face-to-face with Braden's murderer, and, with Soongh's supervision, engaged in an honorable [[Taung blood duel]] that the Hunter won. Unfortunately, the other Mandalorians refused Soongh's demand to let the Hunter finish the Great Hunt in peace, and shot the elderly man in the chest. After the Hunter finished off the rest of Blood's lackeys, with his dying breath, Soongh pleaded the Hunter not to let the Mandalorians fall off the path of honor.<ref name="TOR:HR" />

====The final round====
The last target of the Great Hunt was [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Kellian Jarro]], who was renowned for the most Mandalorian kills during the [[Sacking of Coruscant]]. Crysta instructed the Hunter to eliminate Jarro and disable the Republic cruiser [[Aurora (Valor-class)|''Aurora'']]{{'s}} hyperdrive output regulator, which would cause the ship to be destroyed once it jumps to hyperspace. She also let slip that Blood was already on his way to taking on Jarro.<ref name="TOR:TMK">{{TORcite|type=faction|Bounty Hunter|The Mandalorian Killer|the ''Aurora''}}</ref>

The Hunter located the ''Aurora'' was the Hunter's ship was caught in a [[Tractor beam/Legends|tractor beam]]. Meeting with a Republic security team, the Hunter learned that Blood was captured by Jarro and convinced him that the Hunter was his accomplice. The Hunter refused to be taken into custody and fought through the ship, before finding Blood in the brig. Blood demanded that he be released so they can settle their feud, claiming that it's what both Soongh and Braden would've wanted. Mako retorted that Braden would've wanted to see Blood just as he is, undeserving of an honorable death. The Hunter agreed to leave Blood in his cell and walked away, ignoring the screams of the pathetic former Mandalorian.<ref name="TOR:TMK" />

The Hunter came face-to-face with Jarro on the bridge, who then attempted to use a [[Mind trick/Legends|mind trick]] to subdue the Hunter just as he did Blood, but found that his opponent had a much stronger will. The Jedi then attempted reasoning, stating that there was no profit in revenge but the Hunter wouldn't back down. After the Hunter killed Jarro, his [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Thendys Noori]] encouraged the Hunter to kill her as well, which the bounty hunter did.<ref name="TOR:TMK" />

After narrowly escaping the ''Aurora''{{'s}} destruction,<ref name="TOR:TMK" /> the victorious Hunter returned to Dromund Kaas and was proclaimed a Grand Champion of the Great Hunt.<ref name="TOR:HtCH">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|Hail the Conquering Hero|D5-Mantis}}</ref>

===Grand Champion of the Great Hunt===
None too soon, the Hunter was summoned to [[Mandalore the Vindicated]]'s flagship, the ''[[Spirit of Vengeance]]''. Mandalore commended the Hunter for such honorable actions during the Great Hunt. He then tasked the Hunter to slay Akure, the Beast in the Darkness&mdash;a [[Sithspawn/Legends|Sithspawn]] on Dromund Kaas and bring back a piece of it as a trophy.<ref name="TOR:THoD" />

Returning to the Sith homeworld, the Hunter found a Mandalorian brigade camped outside the beast's cave. Though they warned that no Mandalorian has survived an encounter with the Sithspawn, the Hunter ventured inside. After a long and vigorous fight, the Hunter managed to slay the beast, much to the surprise of the Mandalorians.<ref name="TOR:THoD" />

Returning to the ''Spirit of Vengeance'', the Hunter presented the trophy to Mandalore. Mandalore then revealed this was all a test to see if the Hunter could become a Mandalorian. His reasoning was with the Sith calling on him to fight more wars, he needed a Mandalorian among the Grand Champions. The Hunter accepted membership into his clan. The Hunter and Mandalore then feasted in celebration alongside the other Champions, [[Bloodworthy]], [[Jewl'a Nightbringer]], and the [[Defenestrator]]. The Hunter was then given access to the [[Blacklist]], which was only open to [[Grand Champion of the Great Hunt]].<ref name="TOR:THoD" />

After becoming a Mandalorian, the Champion then went to Taris to deal with the next bounty: [[Jicoln Cadera]], the father of [[Torian Cadera]].<ref name="TOR:AFM">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|A Family Matter|Taris}}</ref>

===The Blacklist===
====Honor or glory====
[[File:Jicoln_Cadera_on_Taris.jpg|thumb|left|260px|Jicoln Cadera, the Blacklist target on Taris]]
Jicoln Cadera had challenged the current Mandalore and lost, going into exile on Taris. Many bounty hunters had tried to locate him and failed, many losing their lives in the process.

With the help of Torian Cadera, who was redeeming his honor as the son of a traitor, the Hunter took Cadera down.

====Product endorsement====
The Hunter got a message from the [[The Adasca BioMechanical Corporation of Arkania|Adasca BioMechanical Corporation]] offering him a product endorsement deal. When they got to [[Quesh]], they unfortunately found that it was a [[Republic Strategic Information Service]] trap organized by a mysterious [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] only seen via holocommunicator.<ref name="TOR:Endorsement">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|Endorsement|Quesh}}</ref>

====Hoth====
The next target on the Blacklist was the legendary Trandoshan Pirate Lord [[Reneget Vause]], who had thrown in his lot with the White Maw.

The Hunter tracked Vause down, but Vause refused to give battle thinking the Hunter unworthy. With the help of Blizz, a jawa betrayed by Vause, The Hunter killed various notable targets until they came to Ki-Ta Kren&mdash;Vause's Blood Brother and White Maw taskmaster.

After defeating Kren, the Hunter finally got to battle Vause and vanquished him.

====Party gone wrong====
[[Bloodworthy]], [[Jewl'a Nightbringer]] and the [[Defenestrator]] booked a private suite in Nar Shaddaa to celebrate the Hunter's victory.<ref name="TOR:Notorious">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|Notorious|Nar Shaddaa}}</ref>

Unfortunately the Republic raided it with [[Adeline Marr]] leading the [[Grand Champions massacre|attack]], directed by the mysterious Jedi master, and killed the three bounty hunters.<ref name="TOR:Notorious" />

===Republic's most wanted===
[[File:JanarusFull-TOR.png|thumb|200px|Supreme Chancellor Dorian Janarus, the most important target on the list of the The Hunter]]
In the wake of its raiding party's defeat, Mako checks the [[HoloNet/Legends|HoloNet]] and comes across a broadcast from [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Dorian Janarus]] himself, condemning the Hunter for the deaths of a delegation of Senators and Jedi on Nar Shaddaa, which was in actuality the Champion's party. The Republic then put the Hunter on the top of its most wanted list, accusing them of a whole kilometer list of crimes, half of which they were not responsible for, and set a ten million credit bounty for their capture. Accusations are flying across the HoloNet and the Empire disavowed the Hunter. The Hunter then turned to the crew for suggestions on where to hide. Blizz suggested they hide with his fellow Jawas and Gault suggested working for the Hutts, the latter of which Torian was opposed to.<ref name="TOR:Notorious" />

Before the two could come to blows, the Hunter received a summons from [[Darth Tormen]] to his vessel the ''Tyrant''. Upon arrival, the Hunter refused to be disarmed and slaughtered his escort, fighting his way to Darth Tormen. Though annoyed at the death of his troops, Tormen cut straight to business. He explained that as [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]] refused Imperial rule, the [[Treaty of Coruscant]] was dissolved and [[Galactic War|war]] has reignited between Empire and Republic. Tormen desired a swift victory by killing Janarus and he was willing to hire the Hunter to do so. He revealed the identity of the Jedi Master, [[Jun Seros (Jedi)|Jun Seros]], the Chancellor's closest advisor. However, both of their enemies were untouchable so long as they remained on Coruscant, but he had a plan to lure them out. However, there were obstacles to remove before they could proceed with the plan. He instructed the Hunter to chase down two Republic targets, capture if possible but only kill if they attempted to escape.<ref name="TOR:AFtC" />

====The ferryman====
The first target was [[Zale Barrows]] on Belsavis, a smuggler who had helped the Republic break the Mandalorian blockade and was ferrying prisoners to the planet. The Hunter tracked him down to a facility where Barrows hid behind an energy wall, safe from both the Hunter and Skadge, a [[Houk/Legends|Houk]] with a grudge against Barrows.

The Hunter disabled the power supply to the energy wall, only to find that Barrows had escaped and Skadge had destroyed the only lead&mdash;Barrows's droid.

Raiding a Republic facility, the Hunter found the necessary materials and manpower to repair the droid and found out that Barrows had escaped to The Tomb, in the deepest reaches of Belsavis.

Chasing Barrows into The Tomb, the Hunter surprised Barrows while he was fighting a Sith operations group sent to free the Dread Masters and defeated him.

====One man up, one man down====
On returning to his ship, the Hunter found that Torian was missing. They had gone to meet an old friend in a cantina.

They then got a message: Torian had been kidnapped and the Hunter had to come to Hoth to save his life.

Going to Hoth, the Hunter was drawn into an ambush by the [[GenoHaradan]], who informed them that bounty hunting was not a game, despite what the Mandalorians thought. The lead kidnapper regretted that the Hunter was so good&mdash;the Overseers would've scouted them out eventually, but the ransom on their head was just too high to miss out on.

====Kuati General====
The next target was [[Thelonia Redrish]], a Republic Kuati General on Voss. Attacking her forces in the field, the Hunter found evidence that she was covertly attacking Imperial forces.

At a Voss hearing, the General disputed the Hunter's word as unreliable, since they were a terrorist and a Mandalorian. The hearing ended with both the Hunter and General Redrish being sent to the [[Shrine of Healing]] to undertake the trials.

At the Shrine, a Voss Mystic attempted to detain the Hunter, convinced by Redrish that he would disrupt the chance at peace with the Gormak. Meanwhile Redrish journeyed to Gorma-Koss and surrendered to the Gormak.

The Gormak king Jokull was not impressed but sympathizers sprang Redrish, who then ventured into the Dark Heart where the Hunter confronted and defeated her.

====Corellia====
With Belsavis and Voss dealt with, the Hunter was then summoned to the ''Tyrant'' as Tormen was mopping up the Rabaan campaign. But upon arrival, the dreadnought was boarded by members of the [[Republic Special Forces Division]]. The Hunter managed to fight off the invaders and regain control of the ship. Tormen soon executed the surviving bridge crew after learning that the captain was dead.

Turning his attention back to the Hunter, Tormen explained his plan to lure in both Seros and Janarus. If Corellia is conquered, the Republic would send in military forces. But if the planet were to secede from the Republic, their enemies would be forced to try diplomacy. The Hunter would track down the three high-ranking resistance leaders, whom Tormen would force into agreeing to sign a compact. As Corellia is officially declared to be under Imperial rule, Janarus would have no choice to but to journey to the founding planet of the Republic to ratify the treaty, but not before Seros convinces him he can rally the Green Jedi to strike back. Tormen was confident that Seros will take to the battlefield instead of acting through proxy as he previously did with the Hunter. He instructed the Hunter to go on ahead while he readied the ''Tyrant''.

The Hunter then traveled to Corellia and met with Tormen's subordinates, who identified the first target, [[Harlon Fane]], Chairman of the Corellian Corporate Council. Fane and other councilors had locked themselves in the council tower and Darth Tormen wanted them present at the signing of a treaty with the Empire.

Breaking into the tower, the Hunter confronted Fane, who attempted to bargain his way out of trouble. The Hunter was willing to consider his offer if he would pay off the giant bounty on his head. However, Fane suddenly went back on his word and activated his personal shield and ordered his security guards to subdue the Hunter. However, his guards were no match for the Mandalorian. Fearing for his life, Fane pleaded to be spared, promising to leave Corellia but the Hunter wouldn't have it, as Tormen needed him. Seeing he had no options, Fane deactivated his shield and surrendered. The Hunter later presented to Tormen Harlon Fane frozen in carbonite.

The Hunter's next task was to get a Selonian representative. As it would be hard to track her down, the plan was to capture members of the invaluable breeding caste. The sept leader [[Shrona Bel-Il]] confronted the Hunter after he had captured 3 members of the breeding caste with shock collars. Defeating her, the Hunter froze her and returned to Darth Tormen.

The last target was Corellia's former Civil Police Commissioner [[Jonah Carter]]. He had rallied CorSec and the civilians of Corellia to defend it against the Empire. Tormen's forces were laying siege to CorSec HQ, meant to hold their positions while the Hunter captures him. Upon confronting the commissioner in CorSec HQ, Carter assumed that the Hunter was sent to kill him and warned the mercenary that the Corellian people will be rioting in the streets as a result. However, the Hunter revealed that killing him is not the objective. Guessing that the Hunter was working for the Empire, Carter grimly reminded the Hunter that their employers are not common criminals but despots. He warned that if he was taken down, Corellia would be forced to bow before the Sith and asked if the Hunter's conscience was wiped clean by their credits. The Hunter stated that it'd be better than Corellians being massacred. Carter then took the opportunity to jump out of the way as his men in the upper levels dropped a flash grenade that briefly blinded the Hunter and their companion. Despite having the initial advantage, Carter and his men were defeated. Acknowledging that he was beaten, Carter told the Hunter that Corellia will outlast the Empire, but his opponent did not care for his idealism and froze him in carbonite.

The Hunter journeyed to [[Capitol Square]] to deliver Carter to Tormen in the Grand Assembly. Once all the representatives had been captured and thawed, Tormen then forced them into signing a treaty signifying Corellia's legitimate secession from the Republic. Prime Minister [[Cal Falcone]] addressed the politicians on Coruscant, demanding that the Supreme Chancellor come to Corellia to ratify the treaty and acknowledge the planet as a member of the Sith Empire. Soon after his announcement, Falcone was executed by Tormen via Force-choke for failing to bring the resistance to heel.

The Hunter then patiently waited before being informed by Tormen that a Republic fleet, led by the ''Founder'', Janarus' flagship, had just arrived in the system. He predicted that Seros would rally the Green Jedi to aid the Republic in one last offensive, giving the Hunter a window to infiltrate the Green Gardens and exact vengeance. Tormen instructed the Hunter to discreetly kill Seros and then recover his effects.

Upon confronting the Jedi battlemaster, Seros refused his fellow Jedi's offer of aid and dispatched them on an unknown task. He then criticized the Hunter for murdering Kellian Jarro and all those sent to capture him, stating that he could've surrender at anytime, instead choosing a path of violence. In turn, the Hunter accused Seros of kill his fellow Champions and framing him for crimes he did not commit. The Jedi admitted that he did use the Hunter as a red herring to expose the Sith's true colors before readying himself for battle and engaged the Hunter. The Hunter ultimately came out victorious and stood over the defeated Jedi. Seros retorted that despite his failure, he had ensured that everything the Hunter had accomplished had been undone. Refusing to let Seros have the last laugh, the Hunter taunted that Janarus was next, and that Seros had led him right to his death, before fatally shooting Seros, letting him die with regret.<ref name="TOR:Reckoning">{{TORcite|type=faction|Bounty Hunter|Reckoning|Corellia}}</ref>

The Hunter then returned to the Grand Assembly, where Tormen was fighting off a group of Green Jedi and assisted the Sith against them. Once the dust had settled, the Hunter presented Seros' effects, which included a datapad with all the necessary information to reach the Supreme Chancellor.<ref name="TOR:Reckoning" />

====End of the hunt====
The Hunter then returned to his ship, where Tormen laid out a plan for the Hunter to steal a Republic transport, the ''[[Firewing]]'', to board the ''Founder'', whilst being chased by Imperial fighters to fool the Republic into thinking the Hunter's ship was a friendly ship under Imperial fire. Once aboard, the Hunter would destroy any and all space-capable ships to prevent Janarus from escaping and then fight through the Supreme Guard to get to him.<ref name="TOR:NOwaB">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|Number One with a Bullet|Corellia}}</ref>

The Hunter followed through this plan to the letter, eventually reaching the Supreme Chancellor. Once confronted, Janarus requested that he be allowed to speak. He revealed that he had just discovered the immense cost of the operation to apprehend the Hunter and condemned Seros' abuse of power in his vendetta against the Hunter. He didn't condone the Hunter's actions but he understood that bounty hunting was their job. Janarus explained that he had already declassified the Hunter and Seros' actions to the public, clearing the Hunter's name of the false crimes, thus creating a political maelstrom that would effectively result in his removal from office. He offered to grant the Hunter immunity for their true crimes in exchange for assassinating Tormen, revealing that the Hunter's employer had been performing massacres on Corellia and Rabaan and Janarus wanted to prevent him from gaining more power. The Hunter refused and killed Janarus.<ref name="TOR:NOwaB" />

The Hunter then met Tormen aboard the ''Tyrant'', who declared that the two of them had just made their place in history and said he would later require use of the Hunter's skills, to which the Hunter agreed, on the condition that his credits were good.<ref name="TOR:SPJNK">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|Some People Just Need Killing|The Tyrant}}</ref>

===Makeb===
{{Quote|Yeah, Blizz go there with old boss because Imp-people want ice “topes.” Blizz not think it much like ice here though.|Blizz on the Hunter’s mission to Makeb.|<ref name="Little Boss" />}}
In [[3638 BBY]],<ref name="TOR_updates">{{TOR_updates|2.0}}</ref> the Hunter was hired by the Empire to travel to [[Makeb]] during its [[Conquest of Makeb|conquest]] by the [[Hutt Cartel/Legends|Hutt Cartel]] in order to procure [[Isotope-5]].<ref name="TPtH">{{TORcite|exp=rothc|type=faction|Imperial|To Pierce the Heavens|the Vaiken Spacedock}}</ref> When a [[Groundquake/Legends|groundquake]] hit during the mission, Blizz lost an advanced device that he used for torturing [[Jreely Toomb]].<ref name="Little Boss">{{TORcite|exp=kotfe|type=general|Little Boss|Hoth}}</ref>

===Rishi===
[[File:Thera_Markon_on_Rishi.jpg|thumb|left|150px|Thera Markon meets the Hunter on Rishi.]]
During the Hunter's travels in [[Rishi/Legends|Rishi]], they were contacted by [[Thera Markon]], daughter of [[Crysta Markon]], their handler during the Great Hunt. Thera told them that Crysta was killed by the [[Kanawyn Syndicate]] and that she was issuing a bounty on them. After the Hunter took care of the Syndicate, Thera expressed a desire to use their influence with the Empire to expand her smuggling business to [[Dromund Kaas/Legends|Dromund Kaas]], to which the Hunter agreed.<ref name="TOR:TOLB" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|The less time you and trouble spend together, the better."<br />"You've got a ''marvelously'' camouflaged sense of humor, you know that?|Scree and Gault Rennow|<ref name="TOR:LS">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|Light Sleeper|the D5-Mantis}}</ref>}}
The Grand Champion, like many other bounty hunters, was a gruff, unpredictable character with a dark sense of humor. The hunter consistently chose the most ruthless tactics to claim their bounties, and often brought in their bounties dead. They used an extensive array of weapons, including [[Wrist rocket/Legends|wrist rockets]], [[Flamethrower/Legends|flamethrowers]], dual [[Blaster pistol/Legends|blaster pistols]], explosive and electro darts, [[Jetpack/Legends|jetpack]] rockets, [[electroshock net]]s, tracer and heat-seeking missiles, retractable wrist blades, and many others.
{{Endgame}}

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Hunter_and_Torian.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Female bounty hunters can romance Torian Cadera.]]
This article represents the character story of the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|Bounty Hunter]] player class in ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'', a video game from [[LucasArts]] and [[BioWare]]. As a result of being player-determined, no canonical description of this individual is currently available; therefore, the article presents the subject's gender as neutral. Additionally, at various points in the course of the game, the player may choose options different from those described in this article.

The male Bounty Hunter is voiced by [[Tom Spackman]] and the female Bounty Hunter is voiced by [[Grey Griffin|Grey DeLisle]]. Scree can by default be a [[Chiss/Legends|Chiss]], [[Cyborg/Legends|Cyborg]], [[Human/Legends|Human]], [[Rattataki/Legends|Rattataki]], or [[Zabrak/Legends|Zabrak]].

According to [[Hall Hood]], the writer in charge of maintaining consistency throughout the Republic storylines, the decision to make the Bounty Hunter an Imperial class was inspired by [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett's]] employment by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] in the [[original trilogy]].<ref name="TORWars">{{WebCite|url=http://torwars.com/?powerpress_pinw=63654-podcast|text=TORWars Podcast #98: Our Interview with BioWare's Hall Hood|author=J.W. Hollis|date=2012-08-22|format=MP3|archivedate=20131031154130}}</ref>
